Prealgebra · Lesson 4.1

What a Fraction Means

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Every division so far came out clean. Now split 33 bars of clay among 44 friends. Whole numbers cannot do it, since handing out one bar each leaves the fourth friend with nothing. But a fair share clearly exists somewhere between the whole-number marks, so we need a new kind of number.

Problem
Two campers share one strip of dried mango by making a single cut at the middle, giving each person an equal piece. The amount one camper holds is 1÷21÷2. Write that share as a fraction a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • A fraction a/ba/b records one simple idea, the bottom number bb is how many equal parts the whole was split into and the top number aa is how many of those parts the camper is holding. Look at the strip after the single cut and read off those two counts, how many equal pieces there are and how many one camper walked away with.
Show the full solution
One cut at the middle makes 22 equal pieces, and each camper takes 11 of them. That share is 1/21/2​ of the strip. The bottom number says how many equal parts the whole was cut into, and the top says how many of those parts you hold. So 1÷21÷2 has a finished answer, and the answer is 1221​.
Problem
A workbench has 55 equal color bands, and blue tape covers 22 of them. The 55 counts equal pieces in the whole, and the 22 counts how many the tape covers. Write the fraction as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • The two numbers do different jobs. One of them sets the size of a piece by saying how many equal pieces it takes to rebuild the whole bench. The other just counts how many of those equal pieces the tape actually sits on.
  • The bottom of the fraction is how many equal pieces make one whole, which is 55. The top is how many of those pieces you have, which is 22. Stack the count over the size.
Show the full solution
The bench is cut into 55 equal bands, so one band is one fifth of the bench. The tape sits on 22 of those bands, which is 2/52/5​. The two numbers do different jobs. The bottom one sets the size of a piece by saying how many equal pieces make the whole, and the top one just counts how many of those pieces you have.
Problem
Three clay bars are shared equally among 44 friends. Slice every bar into 44 equal strips, deal one strip from each bar to each friend. Write each friend's share as a fraction a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • Count what one friend actually walks away with. They took a strip from the first bar, a strip from the second, and a strip from the third. How many strips is that, and how big is each one compared to a whole bar?
  • Each friend ends up with 33 strips, and each strip is 1441​ of a bar. Three quarter-bars stacked together is 14+14+1441​+41​+41​. Write that as a single fraction a/ba/b.
Show the full solution
Cutting each of the 33 bars into 44 equal strips gives 3×4=123×4=12 strips, and 12÷4=312÷4=3 strips per friend. Each strip is 1441​ of a bar, so one friend's pile is 14+14+14=34.41​+41​+41​=43​. Each share is 3/43/4​ of a bar. So 3÷43÷4 never gets stuck with a leftover. The bar in 3443​ is the division sign, and the fraction is the finished answer.
Problem
A chocolatier pours 77 scoops across 44 trays. Each tray holds 7÷47÷4, and the same amount can be found by counting quarter-parts on one tray. Write that amount as a fraction a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • Try the two readings side by side and see if they really collide. Sharing means 7÷47÷4. Counting quarter parts means asking how many pieces of size 1441​ it takes to build up all 7 scoops on one tray. Both are describing one tray, so both should land on the same number.
  • Seven whole scoops, each cut into 4 quarter parts, gives 7×4=287×4=28 quarter parts in total, spread fairly over 4 trays. That leaves 28÷4=728÷4=7 quarter parts on a single tray. Seven pieces each of size 1441​ is 7×147×41​. Now write that as one fraction a/ba/b.
Show the full solution
Sharing gives 7÷4=747÷4=47​ on each tray. Counting quarter parts gives the same amount, since 77 scoops cut into quarters make 7×4=287×4=28 quarter parts, and 28÷4=728÷4=7 of them land on one tray, so a tray holds 7×14=74.7×41​=47​. One tray holds 7/47/4​. The two readings of a fraction always agree. And 7447​ is past 11, so each tray really does hold more than one full scoop.
Key idea
A fraction is one number. The fraction abba​ is the exact answer to a÷ba÷b. The bar is a division sign, not an unfinished problem. There are two ways to read the fraction, and both give the same number. Cut one whole into bb equal pieces and keep aa of them. Or share aa wholes equally among bb people. The bottom number is called the denominator, and it gives the size of one piece by saying how many equal pieces make one whole. The top number is called the numerator, and it counts how many of those pieces you took. A bigger denominator makes each piece smaller.
Problem
A beetle starts at 00 and hops toward 11 in equal steps, landing exactly on 11 after 66 hops. Write the beetle's position after a single hop as a fraction abba​.
Show a hint
  • The whole journey from 00 to 11 got split into 66 equal pieces, one piece per hop. After one hop the beetle has covered just one of those 66 equal pieces of the way to 11.
  • A fraction abba​ tells you to cut the trip to 11 into bb equal parts and take aa of them. Here the trip is cut into 66 equal parts and the beetle has taken 11 of them.
Show the full solution
Six equal hops cover the whole distance from 00 to 11, so a hop of length hh satisfies 6×h=16×h=1. The number that stacks up 66 times to make 11 is one sixth, so after a single hop the beetle sits at 1/6.1/6​. The 66 underneath records that the trip to 11 was cut into 66 equal steps, and the 11 on top records that one of those steps has been taken.
Problem
The beetle hops in steps of 1661​ and makes 55 hops. It ends up past the halfway mark but short of 11. Write the beetle's position after 55 hops as abba​.
Show a hint
  • The denominator tells you the size of one hop, and the numerator counts how many of those hops the beetle has taken. So ask yourself, what is the step size here, and how many steps?
  • Each step is 1661​, and the beetle took 55 of them. Five steps of size one-sixth is 5665​.
Show the full solution
Each step is 1661​ and the beetle takes 55 of them, so it lands at 5×16=56.5×61​=65​. The position is 5/65/6​. Halfway is 33 steps, written 3663​, and 55 steps is more than 33 but fewer than the full 66, which matches a spot past the middle and short of 11.
Key idea
Reading a fraction on the number line. The two numbers in abba​ tell you two different things. The denominator sets the step size. It cuts the distance from 00 to 11 into bb equal pieces, each one a unit fraction 1bb1​ wide, so a bigger bottom means smaller steps. The numerator counts steps. Start at 00, move aa of those steps to the right, and the point you land on is abba​. The steps continue past 11, so a fraction can be bigger than 11.
Problem
Walk 7447​: four quarter-steps reach 11, then 33 more land between 11 and 22. Enter the larger whole number 7447​ falls between.
Show a hint
  • Walk in quarter steps from 00. Four of them stack to 44=144​=1, a whole number you pass through. Where you finally stop is wedged between two whole numbers in a row. The question asks for the larger one.
  • You take 77 quarter steps in all. The first 44 bring you to 11. The remaining 33 carry you past 11 but stop short of 22, because landing on 22 would need 44 more steps and you only had 33. So 7447​ sits between 11 and 22, and the larger of those is the answer.
Show the full solution
Quarter steps land on a whole number every 44 steps, since 44=144​=1 and 84=248​=2. Seven steps clears the checkpoint at step 44 but falls one short of step 88, so 7447​ sits between 11 and 22. The larger of those is 22​. The denominator sets the step size and the numerator counts the steps, so you can place any fraction by asking which multiples of the bottom the top falls between.
Fun fact
The bar in a fraction is the vinculum, introduced by al-Hassar in the 1100s and spread by Fibonacci. It makes 3443​ both the question (3÷43÷4) and the finished answer at once.
Problem
A machine lights a lamp when the top divided by 88 is a whole number. It tries 8888​, 248824​, 408840​, 528852​. How many tops light the lamp?
Show a hint
  • A fraction a88a​ is a whole number exactly when 88 goes into the top aa evenly, with nothing left over. So instead of dividing, just ask of each top, is it a multiple of 88?
  • Walk the multiples of 88 and check each top against them. 88, 1616, 2424, 3232, 4040, 4848, 5656. Now look at 88, 2424, 4040, 5252 one at a time and count how many appear in that list.
Show the full solution
A fraction a88a​ is a whole number exactly when 88 divides the top. The multiples of 88 are 8,16,24,32,40,48,568,16,24,32,40,48,56. Of the four tops, 8=8×18=8×1, 24=8×324=8×3, and 40=8×540=8×5 are on that list, while 52=48+452=48+4 leaves a remainder of 44. So 33​ tops light the lamp. No real division is needed. A fraction is a whole number exactly when the bottom divides the top, which is last chapter's divisibility all over again.
Key idea
Fractions and whole numbers. The fraction abba​ means aa steps of size 1bb1​. You land on a whole-number tick only when those steps fill complete groups of bb with nothing left over, and that happens when bb divides aa evenly. It is the same divisibility test you did last chapter. When the bottom divides the top, the fraction is a whole number sitting on a labeled tick. When it does not, the fraction is a new number between two ticks.
Problem
A diver descends 77 kicks of 1331​ m, landing at −73−37​ m between two whole marks. Which whole number is deeper? Enter it with its minus sign.
Show a hint
  • Walking left from 00, every 33 kicks of size 1331​ add up to one whole meter down. How many full meters can you fit inside 77 thirds before you run out, and how much is left over?
  • 77 thirds is 66 thirds plus 11 more third. The 66 thirds carry her to exactly −2−2, and the leftover third pushes her a little past −2−2 toward −3−3. So she hangs between −2−2 and −3−3. The deeper mark is the more negative one.
Show the full solution
Thirds clump into whole meters three at a time, since 33=133​=1, so −73=−33−33−13=−1−1−13.−37​=−33​−33​−31​=−1−1−31​. The first six thirds carry her to exactly −2−2, and the leftover third nudges her just past it, still short of −3−3. She hangs between −2−2 and −3−3, so the deeper mark is −3.−3​. Left of 00 the numbers get smaller as you go down, so the deeper of two marks is always the more negative one.
Problem
Ava: −125−512​. Ben: 12−5−512​. Cleo: − ⁣(125)−(512​). All claim the same point left of 00. How many distinct points do they name?
Show a hint
  • Don't trust the look of the writing, trust where the walking ends. Carry out each student's instruction as a real trip on the line and mark the spot it stops. Are those stopping spots in different places, or the same place written three ways?
  • The original mark is 1212 backward steps of size 1551​, which is −125−512​. Now check each student. Ava already wrote −125−512​. Ben's 12−5−512​ means 1212 copies of a backward fifth, also −125−512​. Cleo's −(125)−(512​) reflects 125512​ to the other side, again −125−512​. Count how many different landing spots that gives.
Show the full solution
All three write the same number. Ava has −125−512​ outright. Ben's 12−5−512​ is 1212 backward fifths, and flipping the sign of the bottom flips the sign of the quotient, so 12−5=−125−512​=−512​. Cleo's −(125)−(512​) reflects 125512​ across 00, landing at −125−512​ too. They name 11​ point. A single minus sign has three legal homes, out front, on top, or on the bottom, and none of them changes where you land.
Key idea
Sign placement in a fraction. One minus sign can sit in three places. It goes on top as −abb−a​, on the bottom as a−b−ba​, or in front as −ab−ba​. All three land on the same point to the left of 00, so they are one number written three ways. The usual habit is to put the minus in front so the top and bottom stay positive. Two minus signs are a different case. A negative top and a negative bottom cancel, so the fraction is positive.

Keep the top number fixed and let the bottom run through 1,2,3,…1,2,3,…. Counting how many of those bottoms make the fraction a whole number is the same as counting the divisors of the top, so this is the divisor counting from last chapter.

Problem
A pogo stick hops 1881​ m, and a flag marks every whole-meter landing from hop 11 to 4040. How many of the 4040 hops plant a flag?
Show a hint
  • After nn hops the stick is at n88n​ of a meter. A flag goes in only when that position is a whole number. So you are looking for the counts nn that make n88n​ come out even, with nothing left over.
  • The fraction n88n​ is a whole number exactly when nn is a multiple of 88. Just count the multiples of 88 that sit in the range from 11 to 4040.
Show the full solution
After nn hops the stick rests at n88n​ of a meter, which is a whole number exactly when nn is a multiple of 88. Between 11 and 4040 those are 8,16,24,32,408,16,24,32,40, so 55​ hops plant a flag. You can skip the listing. The count of multiples of 88 up to 4040 is just 40÷8=540÷8=5.
Problem
Machine places 60nn60​ for n=1n=1 to 5050, with a green light when the result is whole. One divisor of 6060 exceeds 5050. How many values of nn light the lamp?
Show a hint
  • The light comes on exactly when nn divides 6060 evenly, so your real job is to list the divisors of 6060. Find them all first, then look for any that sit outside the range 11 to 5050.
  • Divisors come in pairs that multiply to 6060, like 11 with 6060, 22 with 3030, 33 with 2020, and so on. Count every divisor of 6060, then subtract the ones larger than 5050.
Show the full solution
The marker 60nn60​ is a whole number exactly when nn divides 6060, so hunt the divisors in pairs that multiply to 6060. 1×60,2×30,3×20,4×15,5×12,6×10.1×60,2×30,3×20,4×15,5×12,6×10. That gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 601, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60, twelve divisors. The machine only tries nn up to 5050, and 6060 is the single divisor above that ceiling, so 12−1=1112−1=11​ values light the lamp. Only the largest divisor can break the ceiling here, because its partner is 11, the smallest divisor there is.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A spool is clamped at 99 evenly spaced points, cutting it into 99 equal lengths. The share-reading for one length is the answer to 1÷91÷9. Write it as a fraction a/ba/b.
Show the solution
One coil cut into 99 equal pieces gives each piece 1÷91÷9, and that division is the fraction 1/91/9​. The top number is the one whole coil you started with, and the bottom number is how many equal pieces the clamps made.
Practice
Five sheets of gold leaf are shared equally among 88 picture frames, nothing wasted. Write how much gold leaf one frame receives as a fraction abba​.
Show the solution
Sharing 55 sheets equally among 88 frames is 5÷85÷8, so each frame receives 5/85/8​ of a sheet. That is less than one full sheet, which fits, since 55 sheets cannot give 88 frames a whole sheet each.
Practice
A hose is cut into 77 equal sections. A sticker covers exactly 44 of them. Using the cut-and-take reading, write the fraction of the whole hose the sticker covers as a/ba/b.
Show the solution
The hose is cut into 77 equal sections, so each section is 1771​ of it. The sticker covers 44 sections, which is 44 copies of 1771​, or 4/74/7​ of the hose. The bottom of the fraction is how many equal pieces make the whole, and the top is how many of them you take.
Practice
A beetle reaches 11 in exactly 1212 equal steps, each of size 112121​. How many of these steps does the beetle take to travel from 00 to 11?
Show the solution
A step of 112121​ is one piece out of 1212 equal pieces that fill a whole, so twelve steps cover 12×112=1212=112×121​=1212​=1. The beetle takes 1212​ steps. The step count matches the denominator because the denominator was telling you how many equal pieces make one whole all along.
Practice
A token is 1717 steps of 1551​ out from 00, at address 175517​. It falls between two whole numbers. Enter the smaller of those two whole numbers.
Show the solution
Five steps of 1551​ make one unit, so whole numbers sit at 0,5,10,15,200,5,10,15,20 steps out, which are the addresses 0,1,2,3,40,1,2,3,4. The token is at 1717 steps, between 1515 and 2020, so 175517​ falls between 33 and 44. The smaller is 33​. Checking directly, 3=1553=515​ and 4=2054=520​, and 15<17<2015<17<20.
Practice
A hold sits at height 113311​ m, between two whole meter marks. Enter the larger of the two whole numbers that 113311​ falls between.
Show the solution
Whole meters come in groups of three thirds, since 33=133​=1. Three whole meters use up 9339​, leaving 113−93=23311​−39​=32​, so 113=3+23311​=3+32​. That is past the 33 mark and short of 44, so the larger whole number is 44​.
Practice
A sensor hangs at −94−49​ m, between two whole meter marks. Which whole meter mark is the deeper (lower) of the two? Give it with its minus sign.
Show the solution
Since 94=21449​=241​, the sensor sits at −214−241​, a quarter meter below the −2−2 mark and not yet down to −3−3. The deeper of the two marks is −3−3​ Deeper means more negative, so the lower mark is the one farther from the surface.
Practice
A log reads 84/7 bins. 847784​ lands on a whole number when 77 divides 8484 exactly. Check divisibility. If it does, what whole number does 847784​ equal?
Show the solution
Counting up in sevens gives 7,14,21,28,35,42,49,56,63,70,77,847,14,21,28,35,42,49,56,63,70,77,84, and 8484 lands right on the twelfth step. So 77 divides 8484 with nothing left over, and 847=12784​=12​ bins.
Practice
Four ribbons laid end to end fill 00 to 44. Split that stretch equally among 33 friends. Where does the first friend's piece end? Write that address as abba​.
Show the solution
The stretch from 00 to 44 measures 44 units, and sharing it among 33 friends means 4÷34÷3, so one piece is 4334​ long. The first piece starts at 00, so it ends at address 4/34/3​ That is a little past 11, which makes sense, since 44 split three ways gives each person a bit more than one whole ribbon.
Practice
Three cards on a number line: −83−38​, 8−3−38​, −(83)−(38​). Trace where each points. How many distinct points do they name in total?
Show the solution
Read each card as one signed number. The first is already −83−38​. A positive over a negative is negative, so 8−3=−83−38​=−38​. And −(83)−(38​) is the opposite of 8338​, again −83−38​. All three land on one spot, so they name 11​ point. A minus sign on top, on the bottom, or out front all do the same job, they flip the sign once.
Practice
Five addresses: 805580​, 806680​, 80161680​, 80101080​, 803380​. A locker is real when the fraction is whole. How many are real lockers?
Show the solution
The top is always 8080, so an address is a whole number exactly when its bottom divides 8080. Checking each one, 805=16580​=16, 8016=51680​=5, and 8010=81080​=8 come out even, while 66 and 33 both leave a remainder. That is 33​ real lockers.
Practice
Tiles 7272 into nn equal rows: needs n∣72n∣72. For how many whole numbers n≥1n≥1 does 72nn72​ land on a whole number?
Show the solution
72nn72​ is a whole number exactly when nn divides 7272, so count the divisors of 7272. Hunting in pairs that multiply to 7272 gives 1×721×72, 2×362×36, 3×243×24, 4×184×18, 6×126×12, and 8×98×9, which lists 1,2,3,4,6,8,9,12,18,24,36,721,2,3,4,6,8,9,12,18,24,36,72. That is 1212​ values of nn. Once the two partners in a pair meet in the middle, like 88 and 99 here, you have caught every divisor.
Practice
A loader accepts nn trays when n+7n=1+7nnn+7​=1+n7​ is a whole number, i.e., when nn divides 77. For how many whole numbers n≥1n≥1 does the loader accept the stack?
Show the solution
Split the top. n+7n=nn+7n=1+7n.nn+7​=nn​+n7​=1+n7​. The 11 is already whole, so the whole expression is a whole number exactly when 7nn7​ is. Since 77 is prime, only n=1n=1 and n=7n=7 divide it, giving 81=818​=8 and 147=2714​=2. That is 22​ values of nn.

Learn it by doing it

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
